newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's bourse to list petrochemicals firm.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's bourse to list petrochemicals firm.

text.p: The Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE) has approved the listing of Boubyan Petrochemicals Co (BPC) which has 10 percent of a $2 billion project in Kuwait, a bourse official said on Wednesday.
Trading in BPC shares start on Saturday. The company was established in February 1995 with a capital of 30 million dinars ($99 million).
Its other partners in the $2 billion Equate petrochemicals project are Union Carbide of the U.S. and Kuwait's state Petrochemical Industries Company (PIC) which each own 45 percent.
Equate, which is due to come on stream next month, will make 650,000 tonnes per year of ethylene, 450,000 tonnes per year of polyethylene and 350,000 tonnes per year of ethylene glycol.
BPC reported a net profit of 2.25 million dinars in 1996 during which return on equity was seven percent and return on assets was to 6.9 percent.
The par value of the share is 100 fils. Its book value at the end of 1996 was 107.47 fils. There are 1,000 fils too the dinar.

Trade on the KSE is exclusive to nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates. Foreign residents of Kuwait can paticipate through mutual funds ran by domestic firms.
BPC's listing will raise the number of traded concerns on the Kuwait exchange to 68 companies with a market capitalisation of over $24 billion.
